note: Fixes to the inputs of tools/build-heights.ts, each with its reason. Positions are world x, z (src/geo.ts); a fix applies within reach metres of the line along the given points. A station's height is its platform level; a depth is how far its platform is below the ground over its platform tracks (Lantmäteriet's elevation model).

stations.why: Wikidata's 2.6 m is the street; the platforms are a little higher, a metre above the rail. Where the tracks leave the platforms' south end in the open, Lantmäteriet's elevation model has the track bed at 2.5–2.8 m, and Google Earth's 3D model (tied to the elevation model on Munkbroleden beside it) the rails at 2.6–2.8 m, rising from there on to the bridge to Slussen. The strip at +7 to +7.5 m that the elevation model shows over the platforms is the station's roof, under Centralbron's edge, not a deck the tracks are on.
Wikidata has no height. Swedish Wikipedia's article on the station: the green line's platform is about 18 m under the ground and at 1.3 m above sea level.
Wikidata has no height. Swedish Wikipedia's article on the station: the platform is about eight metres under the ground.
Wikidata has no height. Swedish Wikipedia's article on the station: the platform is about 9 m under the ground.
Wikidata has no height. Swedish Wikipedia's article on the station: the platform is 8 m under the ground.
Wikidata has no height. Swedish Wikipedia's article on the station: the platform is 6–18 m under the ground, but 17 m above sea level.
Wikidata has no height. Swedish Wikipedia's article on the station (infobox): 5 m deep.
Wikidata has no height. Swedish Wikipedia's article on the station: in a rock cavern 19 m under the ground.
Wikidata has no height. Swedish Wikipedia's article on the station: in a rock cavern 25 m under the ground.
Wikidata has no height. Swedish Wikipedia's article on the station (infobox): 5 m deep; the platforms are in a short tunnel under the town centre.

Wikidata has no height, so the platform tracks followed the elevation model, which put the platform 0.9 m low, and the viaduct north of it over Sockenvägen 1.3 m low, 2.8 m over the road where the sign on it says 4,0 m. Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has the platform's surface at 24.45–24.55 m along its open southern half, the ballast beside it at 23.1–23.2 m, the viaduct's top at 23.6 m over Sockenvägen and the road under it at 18.1 m.

Wikidata has no height, so the platform tracks followed the elevation model, which put the platform 0.7 m low. Lantmäteriet's laser scan has the platform's surface at 36.6–36.7 m and the ballast beside it at 35.4 m; the streets under the track deck at the ticket hall are at 32.1–33.0 m.

Wikidata has no height, and the platform tracks came out 2.5 m under the ground, so the station sat in a trench. Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has both platforms' surface at 38.2–38.4 m and the ballast beside them at 36.9–37.2 m, falling a little to the north; Johanneshovsvägen's deck over the platforms' south end is at 42.7–43.5 m.

Wikidata has no height, so the platform tracks followed the elevation model, which put the platform 0.5 m low. Lantmäteriet's laser scan has the platform's surface at 36.7–36.8 m over its southern half and 36.5 m at its north end, the ballast beside it about 1.2 m lower, and the street under the bridge at its south end at 30.2 m.
Wikidata has no height. Swedish Wikipedia's article on the station: 46.2 m above sea level, the third highest station of the metro.

Wikidata has no height, so the platform tracks followed the elevation model, which put the platform 1.1 m high. Lantmäteriet's laser scan has the platforms' surface at 16.2–16.5 m, rising to the east, where the line starts its climb to Tranebergsbron halfway along them, the metro's ballast beside them at 15.0–15.5 m and the Nockebybanan's between them at 15.8–15.9 m. The network's platforms are level, and the climb, at its steepest grade from their end, still holds them 0.6 m above this.

Wikidata has no height, so the platform tracks followed the elevation model, which put the platform 0.45 m low. Lantmäteriet's laser scan has the platform's surface at 41.8–41.9 m at both ends beyond the roof, the ballast beside it at 40.5 m, and the ground at the foot of the retaining walls by the underpass at 37.2 m.

Wikidata has no height, so the platform tracks followed the elevation model, which put the platform 0.5 m low. Lantmäteriet's laser scan has the platform's surface at 31.49 m by Vinjegatan's deck, rising to 31.71 m 90 m on at its open end, and the ballast beside it at 30.35–30.40 m; this is its middle, under the roof.
Wikidata has no height. Swedish Wikipedia's article on the station: in a rock cavern 21 m under the ground, under the old film studios.
Wikidata has no height. Swedish Wikipedia's article on the station: in a rock cavern 28 m under the ground at Hallonbergen's centre.
Wikidata has no height. Swedish Wikipedia's article on the station: in a rock tunnel 20 m under the ground.

Wikidata has no height, nor Swedish Wikipedia a depth: held at the level the line's profile gave it, 30–33 m under the streets at its entrances, before the rails north-west of Kistaviadukten were set from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, which would have pulled it 1.25 m down.

The only one of the blue line's stations in the open, on the viaduct over the bus terminal and Kista Galleria (Swedish Wikipedia). Wikidata's 10 m is neither the platform nor the streets under it (13.2–14.3 m). Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has the platform's surface at 25.45–25.6 m through the openings in its roof, and the tracks' decks beside it at 24.1–24.35 m, level with the viaduct's from 0.7 km south-east of the station to 0.3 km north-west of it; it had been taken to be a storey and a half over the ground, 4 m too low.

Wikidata has no height, and with its tracks taken for tunnels under the decks the station came out 1.3 m under the real one. Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has both islands' surface at 24.85–25.0 m where it sees them past the roofs' edges, and the ballast of the three tracks beside and between them at 23.6–23.75 m; Kirunaplan's deck over the platforms' south-eastern end is at 29.2–30.2 m.

Wikidata's 46.8 m (from the book "Stockholm under", whose height system isn't stated) put the platform 0.6 m under the real one, and the ticket hall's doors above the passage outside them. Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has the platform's surface at 47.36–47.40 m along its open northern part, 47.3 m at its north end, and the ballast beside it at 46.0–46.1 m.

The station came out 1.2 m under the real one, its ticket hall's stairs climbing 5.4 m to a street 4 m over the platform. Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has the platform's surface at 11.04–11.12 m along its open western part and under the roof's edges, the ballast beside it at 9.7–9.75 m, and the street over its east end, Örnsbergsvägen, and the square at the station building's doors at 15.0–15.1 m.

The station came out 0.6 m under the real one. Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has the platform's surface at 19.56–19.70 m along its open western part, the ballast beside it at 18.0–18.4 m, and the footbridge and the square at the station building's doors, on the deck over the tracks' east end, at 22.8–23.1 m. Set at 19.75 m, which the line's smoothing through the cutting, held near the elevation model's ground, brings down to 19.58 m.

Wikidata's 46.1 m (from the book "Stockholm under", whose height system isn't stated) put the platform 0.5 m under the real one, and the deck over Bredängstorget too low over the square. Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has the platform's surface at 46.59–46.67 m along its open western part, the ballast beside it at 45.2 m, the square at the ticket hall's doors at 40.3 m and the roof's top at 50.0 m. Set at 46.75 m, which the line's smoothing along the viaduct brings down to about 46.6 m.

Wikidata's 36.3 m (from the book "Stockholm under") put the platforms half a metre under the real ones. Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has the islands' surface at 36.88–37.03 m, rising a little northwards, the ballast beside them at 35.6–35.7 m, and the ground at Sätra centrum's doors, whose floor the gates are on, at 40.6–40.8 m.

Wikidata's 37.6 m (from the book "Stockholm under") put the platform half a metre under the real one. Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has the platform's surface at 38.41–38.51 m, rising a little eastwards, the ballast beside it at 36.9–37.1 m, the roof's edges at 42.1–42.3 m, and Vårberg centrum's floor, which the ticket hall is on, and the ground north of the station's building at 42.3–42.4 m.

Wikidata's 27.3 m (from the book "Stockholm under") put the platform 0.8 m under the real one. Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2020) has the platform's surface at 28.06–28.21 m along its open north-western part, falling to 27.8–27.9 m south-east of the ticket hall, the ballast beside it at 26.6–26.8 m, the roof's top at 31.2–31.5 m, the square below the bank to the south-west at 22.3 m, and the deck over the northern track at the hall's end at 31.0–31.3 m.

Wikidata's 18.1 m put the platform 1.7 m under the real one. Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2020) has the platform's surface at 19.72–19.83 m along its open south-western end, falling a little north-eastwards, the ballast beside it at 18.4–18.6 m, the roof's top at 23.1–23.3 m, and the floor of the walkway past the ticket hall's doors, over the tracks, at 23.8 m. Set at 19.9 m, which the line's smoothing brings down to 19.73 m.

Wikidata's 31.8 m (from the book "Stockholm under") put the platform 0.7 m under the real one. Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2020) has the platform's surface at 32.7 m on its open western end, the rails beside it falling from 31.5 m there to 31.1 m at the eastern end, the roof's top at 36.0–36.4 m, the ticket hall's roof between the tracks at 33.0 m and the footbridge's at 30.6–30.9 m. The platform is held level: set at its middle's height, 32.45 m.

uncovered.why: Between T-Centralen and Gamla stan the line runs in a trough built in the water and in Riddarholmskanalen, with Centralbron resting on it, not in a bored tunnel under ground. It needs no cover under the water (its depth is under rail, below), and from the canal to the platforms' north end the "ground" above it is Centralbron and Gamla stan's station roof.
Gullmarsplan, south of the platforms: the tracks run on under the bus terminal's deck and Nynäsvägen in a concrete box, not a bored tunnel, so they need no cover of rock.

Gullmarsplan, south-east of the platforms: the southbound track to Skärmarbrink runs under the bus terminal's deck to its portal by Nynäsvägen, at the level of the station's cutting, not in a bored tunnel. The elevation model has the cutting's floor under the deck, at the rails' level, so cover of rock would put the track 6 m under the station and drag the platforms down with it.
Gullmarsplan, south-east of the platforms: the northbound track from Skärmarbrink, under the bus terminal's deck from the same portal as the southbound one beside it.

Vårby gård, south-east of the platform: the northern track runs on from the ticket hall's end under a deck at the street's level, and both tracks then under Vårby allé, in concrete boxes just under the street, not bored tunnels. Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2020) has the deck and the street 4.5–5 m over the ballast beside them, and the southern track in the open to 75 m past the platform's end.

offGround.why: Sockenplan, 50 m south of the platform: the elevation model dips 3 m under the line for about 15 m, where the cycleway along Enskedevägen's park passes under it (OSM: tunnel). Lantmäteriet's laser scan has the bank's ballast falling smoothly from 23.0 m to 21.8 m across it.
Gamla stan, south of the platforms: OSM has the tracks in the open here, but past the quay's edge, a few metres from the platforms, they are on the start of the bridge to Slussen, over the water.
Sätra, the siding beside the running lines north of the station: OSM draws it a few metres into the bank beside them, where the elevation model rises 2–4 m above the track.
Kristineberg, west of the station: the elevation model dips 5–6 m under the line for about 25 m, where a road passes under it. OSM doesn't map the bridge.
Alvik, east of the station: the elevation model dips 5 m under the line for about 30 m, where a street passes under it on the way to Tranebergsbron. OSM doesn't map the bridge.
Farsta, north of the station: the elevation model dips 5 m under the line for about 20 m, where a road passes under it. OSM doesn't map the bridge.
Svedmyra, the platform's north-east half: the ground falls away under it towards the street that passes under the line there, and the platform stands on a bank, level.

Stureby, west of the platform: the line runs on a bank between upright walls, and over the ticket hall on a deck (the viaducts, below), 3.3 m above the streets either side. The elevation model loses the bank where it is this narrow and has the street under the line, which pulled the platform 0.7 m below the laser scan's.

Vällingby, the platforms' covered south-eastern part and the tracks on under the edge of Vällingby centrum: the elevation model leaves out Kirunaplan's deck and the car park's over them and smooths the ground between their edges, 24.1–24.4 m over the tracks, half a metre over the ballast the laser scan sees where they come out (23.6–23.75 m); held to it, the platforms came out a quarter of a metre over their real height.

Vårby gård, the southern track: it runs along the top of the retaining wall over the square to the south-west, and the elevation model has the square under it, 22.2–23.6 m, where the laser scan (2020) has its ballast at 26.6–26.8 m. Held to it, the platform came out half a metre under its real height.

South of Högdalen, the main line's southbound track through the trough under the depot tracks' bridge: the elevation model has the bridge's deck over it, 33.5–34 m, and held to that it rose onto a bank 1.5 m over its ballast either side (the rail entry for it).

rail.why: The trough between T-Centralen and Gamla stan, under the water off Tegelbacken and Riddarholmskanalen: Google Earth's 3D model has the water's surface (0.9 m) right over the line here, with Centralbron's road beside it at about 5 m, so the trough's roof is under the water and its rail about a train's height and a roof below it, level with T-Centralen's platforms. Without this the line climbed straight from T-Centralen and stood above the water in the canal.

The bridge from Gamla stan to Slussen, over Söderström: Google Earth's 3D model, tied to Lantmäteriet's elevation model on Södermalm and Munkbroleden, has its rails climbing from 4 m at Gamla stan's quay to 8 m at Slussen. Bridges get no anchor of their own, so without this the line hung between the stations, level at 6.5–7 m.

South-east of Gullmarsplan, where the tracks to Skärmarbrink come out from under the bus terminal and Nynäsvägen: Lantmäteriet's laser scan has their ballast at 36.1 m at the tunnel's mouth, rising to 38.6 m 50 m on. With the platforms at their real height, the solve otherwise kept the tunnel level and brought the track out 1.6 m above the ground.

Gullmarsplan, south-east of the platforms: the northbound track from Skärmarbrink, on its way to the western platform under the tracks to Globen, runs in its deeper tunnel (OpenStreetMap: layer -3) for 50 m before it reaches them, from the portal it shares with the southbound track. Left to the solve, it rose to within 1.5 m of the southbound track at once, so the two were drawn as one pair in a single tunnel, though OpenStreetMap has them 25 m apart there, and the plan bent them tighter than the line's 200 m curves.

Gullmarsplan, the southbound track to Skärmarbrink in the open gap between the bus terminal's deck and Nynäsvägen's: Lantmäteriet's laser scan has its ballast at 34.9 to 35.25 m there. From the platforms it runs down at about 1.5 % under the terminal, bottoms out in the gap and climbs under Nynäsvägen to its portal; left to the solve, it ran nearly level from the platforms and passed the gap 1 m too high.

Vällingby's middle track, the turnback track between the two island platforms, which no train stops at, and the outer tracks beyond the platforms' ends: the laser scan has the ballast of all three at 23.6–23.75 m, the rail about 0.2 m over it, level with the platforms' tracks (the islands' surface 24.85–25.0 m). Without this the middle track followed the elevation model's ground under the decks and stood 0.4 m over the tracks beside it.

Sätra's middle track, the turnback track between the two island platforms, where no train stops: the laser scan has its ballast at 35.65–35.7 m, as the outer tracks' beside it, so the rail level with theirs (the islands' surface 36.9–37.0 m). Without this it followed the elevation model's ground, and stood 0.4 m over them.

Fruängen, the siding east of the platform to its buffer stop beside the ticket hall: the laser scan has the ballast between it and the platform at 46.0–46.1 m, level with the platform's tracks. Left to the elevation model's ground, which humps up over the retaining wall beside it, it climbed to 1.5 m over them, higher than the platform, at its end.

The bridge over Stocksundet between Bergshamra and Danderyds sjukhus (1978, 230 m, a concrete girder on three piers), and the cutting from it to the tunnel to Danderyds sjukhus: Lantmäteriet's laser scan (March 2021) has the deck's ballast at 14.8 m at its southern end, where the tunnel from Bergshamra comes out of the hillside, rising to 17.2 m over the middle of the sound and falling to 16.2 m at its northern end, and the cutting's ballast falling on to 14.3 m at the tunnel's mouth 65 m further on; the rail about 0.2 m above the ballast. Bridges get no anchor of their own, so without this the line ran straight between the tunnels, 5 m under the deck at its southern end and 4.5 m under it over the water.

Sockenplan's viaduct, its northern 60 m, where it leaves the bank and climbs over a footway and a service road to the square, and the bank north of it, which dips into a shallow sag 50–60 m from the viaduct: Lantmäteriet's laser scan has the ballast at 21.3–21.4 m in the sag, 21.8 m 10 m from the viaduct, 22.3 m at its end and 23.45 m at its northern part's end, and the rail is about 0.15–0.2 m over it. Held only by a clearance over the ground, as the rest of the viaduct is (`raised`), the viaduct's end stood 0.7 m high and lifted the bank north of it 1.1 m over its ballast for 100 m; with no correction at all, the bank stood 0.5 m over it and the viaduct sagged.

Between Rågsved and Högdalen, the southern track from 80 m west of the bridge over the Nynäs railway to 20 m east of the bridge over Magelungsvägen, down the valley between them: Lantmäteriet's laser scan has its ballast falling from 34.5 m to 31.6 m at the railway, 29.25 m at Magelungsvägen's western abutment and 28.8 m at its eastern, and the rail is about 0.15 m over it. With bridges at both ends and no ground anchor near them, the solve carried the line over the valley, 0.5–0.85 m over its ballast from the railway to Magelungsvägen.

Between Rågsved and Högdalen, the northern track, as the southern one beside it (the entry before), on east of Magelungsvägen as far as it stood high: the laser scan has its ballast at 31.7 m at the railway, 29.3 m on the bridge over Magelungsvägen and rising again from 29.0 m east of it to 30.3 m 120 m on. It stood 0.7–1.05 m over its ballast from the railway to Magelungsvägen and 0.3–0.9 m for 120 m east of it.

South of Högdalen, the eastern track to the depot, from 30 m south of where it leaves the line to 90 m past the bridge over the main line and the cycleway: Lantmäteriet's laser scan has its ballast rising from 33.2 m to a crest of 34.3 m over the bridge and falling to 32.7 m, and the rail is about 0.15 m over it. With the bridge between ground anchors 60 m apart, the solve ran nearly level under the crest, 1.1 m under its ballast at the bridge. Held tight (sigma): at a platform's spread the solve smoothed it back down half a metre.

South of Högdalen, the western track to the depot, as the eastern one beside it (the entry before): the laser scan has its ballast rising from 33.1 m to 34.4 m at the bridge over the main line and the cycleway and falling to 32.6 m; it stood 1.0–1.35 m under it there. Held tight (sigma): at a platform's spread the solve smoothed it back down half a metre.

South of Högdalen, the main line's southbound track, from 160 m north-west of the depot tracks' bridge, where it runs through the trough under them beside the cycleway, to 110 m south-east of it: the laser scan has its ballast at 27.9–28.6 m in the trough and rising to 31.5 m beyond, with no points under the bridge's slab. The solve had put it on a bank, 1.3–1.5 m over its ballast at the bridge, leaving 2.5 m between the rail and the slab's underside over it; now 4.3 m. Held tight (sigma): at a platform's spread the solve's smoothing kept it 0.3–0.4 m over its ballast there.

Between Kärrtorp and Bagarmossen, the south-western track over Sockenvägen and Länsmansvägen, from 120 m south-east of the bridge to 70 m north-west of it: Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has the ballast within a metre of the track at 41.15 m at the bridge's south-eastern end and 40.3 m at its north-western, and the rail is about 0.15 m over it. The tracks stood up to 1.05 m under it on the bridge, which sank the bridge's deck into the clearance over the streets; it comes back to the laser's ballast about 120 m and 75 m beyond the ends.

Between Kärrtorp and Bagarmossen, the north-eastern track over Sockenvägen and Länsmansvägen, as the south-western one beside it (the entry before): up to 1.08 m under the laser scan's ballast on the bridge.

Over Skanstullsbron, the eastern track, from Gullmarsplan's platforms through the cutting at the tunnel's mouth under Södermalm to Skanstull's south hall: Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has the ballast on the bridge's deck, within a metre of the track, at 36.8 m at Gullmarsplan (filled in for 60 m under Johanneshovsbron, which hides it from above), still 35.9 m 240 m north of it, then falling to 21.7 m at the bridge's northern end and 20.2 m at the tunnel's mouth, 4% down there, and the rail is about 0.15 m over it. In the tunnel the track is taken on down at 4% and eased onto the platform tracks' level, 16.3 m, 140 m in, under the south hall, whose passages cross over the tracks just beyond the platform's end on floors 3.55 m over it (the station's description). The solve, held only by the stations at both ends, ran the track down a straight slope 4.8 m under the deck in the middle of the bridge and 2 m under the cutting's floor.
Over Skanstullsbron, the western track, as the eastern one beside it (the entry before), on into the tunnel to Skanstull's south hall: up to 5.0 m under the laser scan's ballast on the bridge.

Tranebergsbron (1934, 450 m long, its concrete arch 181 m across Tranebergssund), the southern track, from Kristineberg's platform over the bridge to the street under the line east of Alvik: Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has the ballast within a metre of the track at 18.4 m at the platform's end, 25.6 m at the bridge's eastern end, cresting at 32.1 m over the arch's crown, 25.7 m at its western end and level from there to the street, under the road that crosses over the line west of the bridge (filled in there), and the rail about 0.15 m over it. Bridges get no anchor of their own, so the solve ran the line in an even climb from Kristineberg to Alvik's slope, 3.5 m under the deck at the crown and 2.4 m over it at the western end. West of the street the line falls more steeply than the network's grades allow to Alvik's platforms, so it is left to the solve there, up to 1.1 m under the ballast.
Tranebergsbron, the northern track, as the southern one beside it (the entry before): up to 3.55 m under the laser scan's ballast at the crown and 2.3 m over it at the western end.

West of Alvik, the northern track from where it starts to climb out of the dip west of the station, over the flyover that takes it over the sidings to the depot (OpenStreetMap's bridge starts 36 m before them), down to the bridge over Drottningholmsvägen and on to where it is level with the ground: Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has the ballast at 16.0 m where it starts, 19.4 m on the flyover, 17.5 m over Drottningholmsvägen and 17.9 m at the end, and the rail about 0.15 m over it. Bridges get no anchor of their own, so the solve ran the line in an even climb from Alvik to Stora mossen, up to 2.0 m under the flyover's deck and 0.5 m over the bridge's.

West of Alvik, the southern track from where it passes under Nockebybanan's viaduct (the scan's points there filled in between its ends) to where it joins the northern on the bridge over Drottningholmsvägen and on to where it is level with the ground: the laser scan has the ballast at 15.0 m under the viaduct, 17.5 m over Drottningholmsvägen and 17.7 m at the end, and the rail about 0.15 m over it; the solve had it up to 1.0 m under the bridge's deck.

Between Blackeberg and Råcksta, the eastern track from the end of Blackeberg's platform over the bridge over Björnsonsgatan, down the slope and over the two concrete arches across Kanaans väg and Grimstagatan to where it is level with the ground before Råcksta: Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has the ballast within a metre of the track level at 30.5 m to the bridge over Björnsonsgatan, falling 2.7 % to 25.4 m at the arches' southern end, 24.4 m at their middle and 23.9 m at their northern end, and the rail about 0.15 m over it. Bridges get no anchor of their own, so the solve ran the line in an even fall from Blackeberg to Råcksta, 0.75 m under the ballast at the bridge over Björnsonsgatan and 1.1 m over it at the arches' southern end.

Between Blackeberg and Råcksta, the western track, as the eastern one beside it (the entry before): up to 0.8 m under the laser scan's ballast at the bridge over Björnsonsgatan and 1.2 m over it at the arches' southern end.

Between Råcksta and Vällingby, the northern track where it climbs out of the cutting, over the bridge across the tracks into Vällingby's depot and into the covered stretch beyond it: Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has the ballast at 18.7 m where the climb starts, 21.0 m at the bridge's start, 22.4 m near its end and 22.1 m at the cover's mouth, and the rail about 0.15 m over it. Bridges get no anchor of their own, so the solve had the track up to 1.5 m under the bridge's deck, too low for the trains into the depot under it.

West of Vällingby, the southern track from the bridge over Bräckegatan down into the hollow, over the bridge over Abiskovägen and up the slope to the bridge over Bergslagsvägen east of Johannelund: Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has the ballast at 22.5 m past the bridge over Bräckegatan, 19.9 m at the hollow's bottom, 22.4 m on the bridge over Abiskovägen and 26.4 m before the bridge over Bergslagsvägen, and the rail about 0.15 m over it (the elevation model's ground, which matches the scan to a few centimetres there, filling the 40 m between the scan's two pieces). The solve smoothed the hollow away: 1.2 m over the ballast at its bottom and 0.7 m under it at Abiskovägen. Johannelund's platform is level in the network while the scan has it rising 1.4 m westwards, so the bridge over Bergslagsvägen is left to the solve.
West of Vällingby, the northern track, as the southern one beside it (the entry before): up to 0.6 m over the laser scan's ballast in the hollow and 0.8 m under it at Abiskovägen.

Kymlinge and the bridge over Igelbäcken's valley, the western track, from the tunnel's mouth north-west of the unused station to 16 m short of the one south-east of the bridge: Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021) has its ballast at 21.3–21.5 m along the platform, the deck (its points classed as a bridge's) falling from 21.5 m at the platform's end to 15.7 m at its south-eastern end, and the ballast on to 14.5 m. The rail is 0.3 m over the laser scan's points, as at Kista, whose platform (25.55 m) is 1.3 m over its deck's. The network had it at 24.6–30.4 m, up to 10 m too high: it had the track on a bridge from tunnel to tunnel, held only over the valley's floor.

Kymlinge and the bridge over Igelbäcken's valley, the eastern track, from 8 m north-west of the tunnel's mouth south-east of the bridge to the one north-west of the unused station: the laser scan has its ballast rising from 14.2 m to 15.5 m to the deck, the deck rising to 21.4 m at the platform's end, and the ballast at 21.3–21.5 m along the platform. The rail is 0.3 m over the laser scan's points, as at Kista, whose platform (25.55 m) is 1.3 m over its deck's. The network had it at 15.5–16.6 m, up to 5.4 m too low.

The Ärvinge cutting between the tunnel from Kymlinge and Kistaviadukten, the northern track: the laser scan's ballast (left out under Kymlingelänken's decks). The rail is 0.3 m over the laser scan's points, as at Kista, whose platform (25.55 m) is 1.3 m over its deck's. The network had it up to 0.55 m low.
The Ärvinge cutting, the southern track: as the northern track.

Kistaviadukten, the north-eastern track (but for Kista's platform, which the station's height holds): the laser scan has its deck's points level at 24.2–24.3 m from the Ärvinge cutting to 50 m north-west of the station, then falling to 23.4 m at the viaduct's north-western end. The rail is 0.3 m over the laser scan's points, as at Kista, whose platform (25.55 m) is 1.3 m over its deck's. The network had it 0.2 m high south-east of the station and up to 1.1 m low towards the north-western end.
Kistaviadukten, the south-western track: as the north-eastern track (but for 30 m over the bus terminal's roof at Kista centrum, whose points are classed as the bridge's too).

North-west of Kistaviadukten, the northern track to the tunnel to Husby: the laser scan has its ballast falling from 23.4 m at the viaduct's end to 19.6 m 10 m short of the tunnel's mouth. The rail is 0.3 m over the laser scan's points, as at Kista, whose platform (25.55 m) is 1.3 m over its deck's. The network had it 1.1 m low at the viaduct's end.
North-west of Kistaviadukten, the southern track: as the northern track.

toBridge.why: Hjorthagen, the north end of the bridge from Gärdet: the abutment stands on the hillside, and the 35 m of track from it to the mouth of the tunnel to Ropsten is in a shallow cutting, not on a bank up to the bridge. Without its ground the line had nothing to hold it between the bridge and Ropsten, and humped 5 m over the ground at the mouth.

viaducts.why: Kristineberg: west of the platform both tracks stand on concrete decks over the ticket hall and over Nordenflychtsvägen, which passes under the line and Drottningholmsvägen beside it, and OSM doesn't map them as bridges. Lantmäteriet's laser scan has the decks from 121 m west of the platform's middle to 82 m (the northern track's, over the hall) and 89 m (the southern track's, with the road's), and the street 5.3 m under the platform between 116 m and 96 m; photographs show the underpass's deck on round columns.

Svedmyra: from the ticket hall north, the platform and both tracks stand on a concrete viaduct, which OSM maps as a bridge only where it crosses Tussmötevägen. Lantmäteriet's laser scan has the street 6 m under the platform right up to the deck's edges (6.5 m east and 11 m west of the platform's middle), the elevation model has no bank there, and photographs show bicycles parked under the deck between its columns.

Stureby: west of the platform, over the ticket hall and the footway under the line, both tracks stand on a concrete deck, which OSM doesn't map as a bridge. Lantmäteriet's laser scan has the deck's sharp edges 2.5 m outside the tracks, with the streets 3.3 m below the ballast right up to them, and photographs show the hall's windows and doors and parked bicycles under it.

Brommaplan: from the platform's west end both tracks stand on concrete decks over the ticket hall, which lies under them and between them at the square, and OSM maps them as bridges only from the hall's front west. Lantmäteriet's laser scan has the decks (its points classed as a bridge's) from the platform's end, the hall's floor 6 m under the platform through the glass vault between them, and the wings either side roofed 3.4 m under it; photographs show the hall's doors under the decks and the square running on under them.

Brommaplan, from 140 m to 165 m west of the station's decks: OSM's bridges end 23 m short of the viaduct's western end. Lantmäteriet's laser scan has the deck's points (classed as a bridge's) on to 168 m, over open ground 4–6 m under the rails where it rises to the abutment, and photographs show the viaduct's piers on to there.

Åkeshov: east of the platforms all three tracks stand on concrete decks over the ticket hall and the footway and cycleway passing under the line, from 88 m east of the platforms' middle to 110 m, and OSM doesn't map them as bridges (the correction runs from 74 m to 126 m, the least the track's 10 m samples keep as a bridge; the station draws the bank's ends under them). Lantmäteriet's laser scan has the hall's flat roofs between the decks 0.5 m under the platform, the forecourt 5.5 m under it from the hall's south wall to the underpass's mouth, and the decks over the underpass; photographs show the hall's glass front under them and the underpass's mouth under the southern deck. (The line runs along each track in turn.)

raised.why: Sockenplan's viaduct north of the platform, from 50 m south of the bank to the platform, over Sockenplan, Sockenvägen and the paths and parking beside them (OpenStreetMap: bridge). Bridges get no anchor of their own, so it sagged from the bank north of it to the platform, 1.3 m under Lantmäteriet's laser scan, whose points on the deck are 5.3–5.4 m over Sockenvägen and the square south of it (18.1 m); the sign on it over Sockenvägen says 4,0 m. Its northern part is held in `rail`.

Kistaviadukten, 1,120 m long (Swedish Wikipedia): the line crosses Kista on it, over streets and the bus terminal. Bridges get no anchor of their own, so without this it sagged below the valley's floor south of the station. North of the station the ground rises to the line by itself.

Hjorthagen, between Gärdet and Ropsten: the line comes out of the rock face below Gärdet on to a 300 m concrete beam bridge (OpenStreetMap: bridge, layer 2) over Tegeluddsvägen, Lidingövägen and the ramps of Norra länken, and goes into the hill again before Ropsten. Bridges get no anchor of their own, so without this it ran level from Gärdet's platforms at the height of the tunnel, 3 m under the ground at the streets. Not held at the ends, where the ground rises to the mouths.

stacked.why: Gullmarsplan, south of the platforms: the northbound track from Skärmarbrink passes under the two tracks to Globen (OpenStreetMap: layer -3 under -2) about 70 m from the platforms' south ends, which the laser scan puts at 38.3 m. Held level that far, the tracks can part by only about 5.2 m at the line's gradient, so with the usual 6.5 m the junction dragged the whole station 2.5 m down. Concrete boxes with a thin slab between them need about 5 m: a C20 is 3.7 m tall over the rail.

walled.why: Vårby gård: the southern track runs along the top of a concrete retaining wall 5.5–6.8 m high, over the square and the cycleway south-west of the station, from its mouth under Vårby allé to the bridge north-west of the platform (Lantmäteriet's laser scan: the ballast at 26.2–26.8 m, the wall's top at 27.6–28.2 m, its foot at 21.2–22.7 m; south-east of the ticket hall the ground behind it rises to the street, 31 m). The elevation model smooths the wall into a slope, which made the track an embankment whose bank spread out over the square.

The cutting from the northern end of the bridge over Stocksundet to the mouth of the tunnel to Danderyds sjukhus, 65 m: the tracks run down between concrete retaining walls with ribbed faces, the hillside behind the western one 2–4 m above the ballast and a street beside the eastern one (Lantmäteriet's laser scan; photographs on Wikimedia Commons). Laid on the laser scan's ballast (the bridge's rail heights, above), the line is level with the elevation model's ground there, which smooths the walls away, so it was drawn on the ground.
